title: Lower limb theory · report dated 17 April 2021
note: TUMS report TestId 20333. The report date is 17 April 2021; this does not independently establish the sitting date.

questions.prompt: Which of the following muscle has dual nerve supply:
questions.note: Pectineus is mainly femoral-supplied and may also receive obturator/accessory obturator supply; dual supply is variable, not obligatory.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following does not pass though the greater sciatic foramen?
options: the posterior cutaneous nerve of the thigh
questions.note: The nerve to obturator externus comes from obturator nerve via the obturator canal, not the greater sciatic foramen.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All the following are branches of the femoral nerve except:
questions.note: Lateral femoral cutaneous is an independent lumbar plexus branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which one of the following muscle is inserted into adductor tubercle of femur:
questions.note: The hamstring part of adductor magnus inserts on the adductor tubercle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The following muscle is NOT responsible for hip flexion:
questions.note: Vastus lateralis does not cross the hip. Rectus femoris does.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The 1st toe cleft is supplied by
questions.note: Deep fibular nerve supplies the dorsal first interdigital web; plantar surfaces have plantar nerve supply.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: What type of joint is hip joint:
questions.note: The hip is a synovial ball-and-socket joint.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which part of quadriceps femoris has attachment to the hip bone?
questions.note: Rectus femoris has origins at AIIS and the supra-acetabular region.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: A 45-year-old man has trouble walking. At his physician's clinic, when he is asked to stand on his right foot, his left hip drops. Which of the following nerves is most likely damaged, causing his problem:
questions.note: During right single-leg stance, the right abductors stabilize the left pelvis. Right superior gluteal injury produces this Trendelenburg sign.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The lateral sural nerve is a branch of which of the following nerves?
questions.note: Lateral sural cutaneous branches from common fibular nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Contents of the femoral sheath include:
questions.note: The femoral artery and vein lie in the sheath; femoral nerve is outside it.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Profunda femoral artery is normally the vessel of supply:
options: To the anterior muscles of thigh
To the lateral muscles of thigh
To the medial muscles of thigh
To the posterior muscles of thigh
questions.note: Perforating profunda branches are the main posterior-thigh supply, but profunda also supplies anterior and medial thigh. The broad source wording makes A, C and D defensible; all are accepted.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: At the subtalar/talocalcaneal joint the primary movements are
questions.note: Inversion and eversion are composite hindfoot movements involving subtalar and transverse tarsal joints.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which is not a component of the 2nd layer of the foot
questions.note: Adductor hallucis is in the third layer. Quadratus plantae, lumbricals and long flexor tendons are in the second.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Obturator nerve is divided into anterior & posterior divisions by:
questions.note: In the thigh, adductor brevis separates anterior and posterior obturator divisions. The posterior division has a proximal relationship to/through obturator externus; the source omits the level. A is the standard thigh answer, and the supplied D is retained as a qualified proximal interpretation.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following muscles is the strongest dorsiflexor and invertor of the foot?
questions.note: Tibialis anterior dorsiflexes and inverts the foot.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The most medial structure passing under the inferior extensor retinaculum of the foot is:
questions.note: Tibialis anterior tendon is the most medial listed structure under the extensor retinacula.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a border for TIBIA:
questions.note: The tibia has anterior, medial and interosseous/lateral borders; posterior is a surface.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: A 20-year-old college student receives a severe blow on the inferolateral side of the left knee joint while playing football. Radiographic examination reveals a fracture of the head and neck of the fibula.Which of the following nerves is damaged:
questions.note: Common fibular nerve winds around the fibular neck.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Medial plantar nerve does NOT supply:
questions.note: Adductor hallucis is supplied by the deep lateral plantar branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following attach to the greater trochanter except
questions.note: Iliacus inserts with psoas at the lesser trochanter, unlike the other greater-trochanter attachments.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which structure is intrasynovial at the knee joint:
questions.note: Menisci project into the synovial joint cavity. Popliteus tendon and cruciates are intracapsular but extrasynovial. The supplied mark is corrected.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Floor of the femoral triangle EXCLUDES:
questions.note: Iliopsoas and pectineus form the principal floor; adductor longus may contribute medially, not adductor brevis.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Difficulty extending the knee can result from damage to the
questions.note: Quadriceps is femoral-supplied and extends the knee.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a content of the adductor canal?
questions.note: The femoral nerve trunk is not in the adductor canal. Saphenous nerve is; nerve-to-vastus-medialis relations depend on fascial definition.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The muscle that unlocks the knee joint is
questions.note: Popliteus unlocks the knee: medial tibial rotation when free, lateral femoral rotation when weight-bearing.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which of the following is found superficially immediately anterior to the medial malleolus?
questions.note: Great saphenous vein passes anterior to the medial malleolus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Illiotibial tract is inserted on:
options: Upper smooth part of tibial tuberosity
Lower roughened part of tibial tuberosity
questions.note: The IT tract inserts on Gerdy’s tubercle on the anterolateral tibial condyle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The femoral nerve is formed by the posterior division of the anterior rami of:
questions.note: Femoral nerve derives from posterior divisions of L2–4 ventral rami. The supplied mark is corrected.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Posterior tibial artery
options: Divides superior to the flexor retinaculum
Branches form 2 plantar arches in the foot
Divides into the medial and lateral plantar branches
Lateral palmar branch supplies the big toe
questions.note: Posterior tibial terminates as medial and lateral plantar arteries.
questions.subject: anatomy

audit.method: Native text + rendered source inspection; independently reviewed anatomical answers and course-section mapping.
